children.text: As the CTO for the Vermont Agency of Digital Services, my mandate is clear: we must engineer a healthcare infrastructure that is fiscally sustainable and technologically liquid. The legacy 'Silo' model, where patient data is trapped in proprietary vendor-locked repositories, is the primary driver of administrative friction and clinical inefficiency in the State of Vermont.
I. The Strategic Imperative: Data Sovereignty

A central goal of Vermont's 2026 health-data strategy is to sharply increase real-time clinical data liquidity, reducing the 'friction tax' of manual records retrieval across the state's rural health districts.

The shift toward data sovereignty is not merely a technical upgrade; it is an economic necessity. When clinical data becomes liquid, the cost of care coordination drops exponentially. This phenomenon, which I define as 'Technical Deflation,' allows the State to reinvest capital into frontline medical services rather than back-end IT maintenance.

children.text: We are not in the business of buying software suites; we are in the business of engineering public health outcomes. In 2026, a static clinical record is a liability. A liquid record is a life saved.

The transition to Value-Based Care (VBC) requires a technical foundation that can handle real-time risk adjustment and population health analytics. The video analysis below details our trajectory for the next four fiscal years.

children.text: The 2026 Roadmap represents a commitment to the citizens of Vermont. By leveraging technical deflation, we are ensuring that the Agency of Human Services remains a global leader in health transformation. The data liquidity fabric is no longer a concept; it is the operational reality of our State.

summary: This definitive roadmap outlines the transition of the Vermont Agency of Human Services toward a data-sovereign, FHIR-native interoperability layer. It details the technical deflationary dividends expected from decommissioning legacy Silos and the resulting impact on rural critical access hospital sustainability.
title: The Economic Architecture of Vermont’s 2026 Health Transformation: From Silos to Liquidity Fabrics
